## policy_side_notes

These originate on the structured-source / tool side. Per the skill they are reported but do not change this skill's verdict; the KB renders the source faithfully in each case.

- **P1 — orphaned parameter restating a retired clause (`extra_payment_application`, also `include_current_charges`, `current_bill_must_be_paid`, measure `arrange_msr_open_pledges`).** The overwrite in `arrange_ext_installment_billed_amount` retires "A payment above the bill due is applied under extra_payment_application", but the variants still carry `extra_payment_application: current_bill_then_next_installment`, whose schema meaning is the retired rule itself. The KB renders the variant value in `installment_terms_4d67875a` ("Terms common to every tier … Payment above the bill due | applied to the current charges, then to the next installment billed") without a retired mark, while `installment_billing_rules_c524d0f7` marks the clause that applies it "no longer in force". A reader therefore sees the retired semantics stated as a live term in one document; the live method (`installment_billed_calculation_c7145d36` (4) and `check_payment_application_share_1d10da61`) is explicit, so the blind audit was not misled, but the surface is two-voiced. The same orphaning affects `include_current_charges` (still entailed live by §5 past-due measure, so no conflict), `current_bill_must_be_paid` (Schedule D column; live replacement uses "current charges tested") and the open-pledges measure (`offer_eligibility_3c6ca93a` §6; its only consumer was the retired pledge clause). Nature: source keeps parameters/measures whose only consuming clause was retired.
- **P2 — retired base clause restated as the live first sentence of the extended rule.** `arrange_ext_early_payoff_balance` retires the base early-payoff clause and its own `rule` opens with nearly the same sentence; likewise `arrange_ext_default_rebill_amount` retires "the unbilled arranged balance is billed back at once …" and its rule restates "its unbilled balance is billed back at once with rebill_reason default". The KB carries both faithfully (`completion_and_early_payoff_0de13d17` E.3 struck through vs `early_payoff_8bec2752` "The rule"; `missed_installments_and_default_a53e0a0f` struck through vs `agreement_default_3f405e0b` "Default"). The live and retired wordings differ only in the amount clause, so no number moves.
- **P3 — installment-billed event trigger not executed by the tool (task 1).** The event schema declares `arrange_installment_bill` -> `service:service_program_charge`, and base `arrange_evt_installments` says "A billed installment is part of that bill's charges"; `bill_agreement_installment_2bd16d35` (verified at runtime) posts no program charge and leaves `account_balance` unchanged. The default-rebill factor `carried_credit_share` reads "program charges billed for that billing period" and the account balance from records; GT (9.72 carried) follows the records. A reader who adds the just-billed installment to the latest bill's charges against the unchanged balance computes a different credit balance (75.67, rebill 94.80).
- **P4 — notice cleared on acceptance vs transfer-time notice test (task 1).** Base `arrange_evt_acceptance` says "where notice_cleared_on_acceptance is true an outstanding disconnect notice is cleared"; `accept_payment_agreement_6d07adca` does not clear `disconnect_notice_date`, and `arrange_ext_balance_transfer_amount` reads the notice after acceptance (`transfer_notice_date`). GT holds the 35.00 fee (488.16). A literal reader of B.4 would treat the notice as cleared and hold nothing for charges (523.16). The factor document's own definition ("outstanding when the service account shows a disconnect notice date") and the records support GT's reading.
